pairs.subject: agent-memory
pairs.evidence: src/stores/slices/overview/memorySlice.ts:192 The merge door writes one new row and the backend hard-DELETEs both originals in the same transaction (memories.rs:1662/1666). Nothing is marked superseded or archived, and no tombstone or lineage link is written, so the merged belief cannot enumerate what it replaced and a bad merge cannot be audited or undone.

techniques.evidence: src/stores/slices/overview/memorySlice.ts:192 The technique requires that the members remain, linked, auditable and out of default reads. Here the members are destroyed even though a non-default archive tier exists (:121).

src-tauri/db/src/repos/core/memories.rs:1662 Deletion is supposed to be reserved for redaction. The merge goes straight to DELETE with no archive and no tombstone, although the single-delete path does write a fact tombstone (memories.rs:1430-1436).
src-tauri/db/src/repos/core/memories.rs:1666 The technique says supersede, don't replace. The second original is removed instead of being marked superseded-by the merged id, so the lineage is lost.

src-tauri/db/src/repos/core/memories.rs:1581 The write door re-checks that both members share one persona scope. The merged row takes its persona from its members (:1604), not from the caller's input.
src/stores/slices/overview/memorySlice.ts:263 The LLM reflection pass only proposes. Live rows change only when the user applies a proposal.

pairs.subject: agent-memory
pairs.evidence: src/features/plugins/dev-tools/sub_skills/analytics/CoveragePipeline.tsx:70 Coverage per context is counted client-side from one capped list. The backend clamps the requested 500 to MAX_LIST=50 and orders by updated_at DESC, with no 30-day filter. Any context outside the 50 most recently updated nodes reads as 0 (uncovered) and gets dispatched again, a context with only old nodes reads as covered, and the cut is never reported.

techniques.evidence: src/features/plugins/dev-tools/sub_skills/analytics/CoveragePipeline.tsx:30 The instrument claims a 30-day freshness count but actually measures membership in a global newest-50 window, so a zero does not mean the context is uncovered.
src-tauri/src/commands/infrastructure/memory_ledger.rs:652 The cap silently cuts 500 down to 50. No notice reaches the reader saying content was truncated.

pairs.subject: agent-memory
pairs.evidence: src-tauri/src/commands/infrastructure/memory_health.rs:213 A team-bound project with zero live memories writes no snapshot (only a scan-summary counter), and memory_health_overview returns only each project's latest snapshot. A never-populated project is missing from the list, and a project whose memories all decayed out keeps serving its last healthy score indefinitely.

techniques.evidence: src-tauri/src/commands/infrastructure/memory_health.rs:213 The empty-corpus case is counted only in the transient scan summary. The persisted overview never names the hole.
src-tauri/src/commands/infrastructure/memory_health.rs:268 The latest-snapshot read gives no notice that a project was skipped or has gone empty since that snapshot.
src-tauri/src/commands/infrastructure/memory_health.rs:100 Staleness is measured against a per-item half-life applied to last access, not a fixed age.
src-tauri/src/commands/infrastructure/memory_health.rs:114 Unconfirmed proposals live in their own table, separate from persona_memories.
src-tauri/src/commands/infrastructure/memory_health.rs:151 The governance pillar penalises the backlog and age of the human-review queue.
